html:
Zubarah is a ruined town on the northwest coast of Qatar that was one of the busiest pearling and trading ports of the Gulf in the late 1700s.

It was founded around the 1760s by families of the Bani Utbah who had moved from Kuwait. From here the Al Khalifa took Bahrain in 1783. The town traded pearls to India and was fought over by its neighbours, and it was sacked in the early 1800s. Its people drifted away, and by the 1900s it lay empty under the sand.

Because nothing was built over it, Zubarah shows the plan of a whole Gulf town of its time: houses, markets, mosques and a wall. It became a World Heritage Site in 2013. Qatar's claim to it fed a long border quarrel with Bahrain.
sum: Zubarah is a ruined town on the northwest coast of Qatar that was one of the busiest pearling and trading ports of the Gulf in the late 1700s.
